title: EU AI Act obligations
description: Questions for the legal and AI owners and evidence checks for AI systems under Regulation (EU) 2024/1689, as amended by the AI Omnibus in force since 27 July 2026. Prohibitions and AI literacy have applied since 2 February 2025 and the transparency rules of Art. 50 since 2 August 2026; the rules for high-risk systems apply from 2 December 2027 (Annex III) and 2 August 2028 (Annex I). Obligations depend on the organization's role and on the system's classification; these rules do not establish compliance.

sources.title: Regulation (EU) 2024/1689, Artificial Intelligence Act, consolidated text
European Commission, AI Act Service Desk, Timeline for the implementation of the AI Act

rules.instruction: Ask the legal owner to classify the AI system as a prohibited practice (Art. 5, applicable since 2 February 2025), a high-risk system (Art. 6 and Annex III) or neither, and to record whether the organization acts as provider or deployer (Art. 3).
rules.verification: Link the recorded classification and role from the change.

evidence.title: Recorded classification of the AI system and the organization's role

rules.manual: Classifying the system and the organization's role is a legal assessment; it is named evidence.

rules.instruction: When the system recruits or selects people, filters job applications, evaluates candidates or informs decisions about workers (Annex III, point 4), ask the legal owner before the team builds it to record whether it is a high-risk system under Art. 6(2) or the documented reasons of an Art. 6(3) exception; the obligations for these high-risk systems apply from 2 December 2027.
rules.verification: Link the legal owner's recorded classification of the employment use, or the Art. 6(3) assessment and its registration where Art. 6(4) requires it.
rules.manual: Whether the use is high-risk under Art. 6(2) or excepted under Art. 6(3) is a legal assessment.

rules.instruction: When the system interacts directly with people, tell them that they are interacting with an AI system unless it is obvious (Art. 50(1), applicable since 2 August 2026).
rules.verification: Show the notice in the interface and in a test of the first interaction.
rules.manual: The notice shows in the interface of a running system.

rules.instruction: Ask the AI owner whether the system generates synthetic audio, image, video or text that Art. 50(2) requires to be marked, and implement machine-readable marking where it applies. Art. 50 has applied since 2 August 2026; a system already on the market before that date has until 2 December 2026.
rules.verification: Check the marking on a generated sample, or link the owner's recorded reason why it does not apply.
rules.manual: Machine-readable marking shows on a generated sample.

rules.instruction: For a high-risk system, whose obligations apply from 2 December 2027 for the systems of Annex III and from 2 August 2028 for those of Annex I, record events automatically over its lifetime (Art. 12) and keep the logs under the organization's control for a period suited to the system's intended purpose and of at least six months, unless Union or national law, in particular on personal data, provides otherwise (Art. 19(1) for providers, Art. 26(6) for deployers).
rules.verification: Run the system in a test and confirm that the expected events appear in the logs, and check that the log retention setting is at least six months or names the law that sets another period.
rules.manual: Logged events and retention settings show in a running system and its log store.

rules.instruction: For a high-risk system, whose obligations apply from 2 December 2027 for the systems of Annex III and from 2 August 2028 for those of Annex I, give the people who oversee it the means to interpret, override or stop its output (Art. 14).
rules.verification: Demonstrate the override or stop control in a test and link the oversight procedure.
rules.manual: The override or stop control shows in a running system and in the oversight procedure.

rules.instruction: For a high-risk system, whose obligations apply from 2 December 2027 for the systems of Annex III and from 2 August 2028 for those of Annex I, the organization provides, update the technical documentation of Art. 11 and Annex IV with the change.
rules.verification: Link the updated technical documentation and the version it describes.
rules.manual: The technical documentation of Annex IV is kept by the provider, often outside the repository.

rules.instruction: Ask the AI owner which measures support the AI literacy of the staff who operate or use the system (Art. 4, applicable since 2 February 2025).
rules.verification: Link the recorded measures, such as the training or guidance given to those staff.
rules.manual: Literacy measures are training and guidance given to staff, outside the repository.
